cli.usage:
Usage: sevdesk-mcp [--profile <name>]
       sevdesk-mcp setup [--add]
       sevdesk-mcp <command>

Without a command, starts the MCP server on stdio.

Options:
  --profile <name>  Use only this profile; execute rejects any other account

Commands:
  setup      Add a sevDesk account; its token goes into the OS keychain
  --help     Show this help
  --version  Show the version

Exit codes:
  {success}  Success
  {failure}  Error while running
  {usage}  Usage error (unknown command or option)
cli.invalidProfileName: Invalid profile name: {profile} (1 to 32 characters: a-z, 0-9 and -)
setup.noTty: setup needs an interactive terminal and has no options for scripts. Without one (CI, Docker), set SEVDESK_API_TOKEN (and optionally SEVDESK_PROFILE) in the environment of the MCP server instead.
setup.intro: This adds a sevDesk account as a profile. Its API token goes into the OS keychain, never into a file.
setup.askProfile: Profile name (1 to 32 characters: a-z, 0-9 and -):
setup.askReplace: Profile {profile} ({company}) already exists. Replace its token and settings? {choices}
setup.notReplaced: Profile {profile} was left as it is.
setup.noKeychain:
No OS keychain is available ({reason}).
setup stores API tokens only there: a token in a plain file can be read by any process and any backup, and it grants full access to the bookkeeping.
Without a keychain (headless Linux, WSL, Docker), set SEVDESK_API_TOKEN (and optionally SEVDESK_PROFILE) in the environment of the MCP server instead.
setup.invalidToken: That is not an API token: it is empty or contains spaces or other invalid characters.
setup.tokenRejected: sevDesk rejected the token (HTTP 401). Copy the whole token from sevDesk again and run setup again.
setup.checkFailed: The token could not be checked with sevDesk: {detail}
setup.unsupportedSystem: This account's bookkeeping system ({version}) is not supported; sevdesk-mcp supports only system {supported}.
setup.askReadonly: Read-only? A read-only profile can read everything but change nothing. {choices}
setup.keychainWriteFailed: The token could not be stored in the OS keychain ({reason}).
setup.configWriteFailed: The token is in the OS keychain (service {service}, account {profile}), but the config file {file} could not be written ({reason}). Fix that and run setup again.
setup.invalidConfig:
{message}
Fix the config file and run setup again.
setup.clientEntry: Add this command to your MCP client: npx -y {package} --profile {profile}
